newsitem.title: USA: Oil union mulls strike at Tosco refineries.
newsitem.headline: Oil union mulls strike at Tosco refineries.

text.p: The Oil, Chemical, and Atomic Workers Union Friday said 900 workers are considering a strike at four California refineries being sold to Tosco Corp March 31.
Tosco agreed to purchase the refineries and other downstream assets from Unocal Corp last November for about $1.4 billion.
"We haven't decided to pull troops out but its certainly a possibility," said Bill McGoveran, director of O.C.A.W's western region.
He said a strike is only an option.

While he acknowledged most of the contractual language has been finalized, he said Tosco and the union disagree on the number of job cuts, which he claims will eliminate 114 positions at three of the four future Tosco plants.
A spokesman for Tosco said the company hoped to reach an agreement and avert a strike.
"We expect to reach an amicable agreement prior to the close," of sale the spokesman said.
Over 900 OCAW employees work at the four refineries, which process 250,000 barrels-per-day of crude.

Tosco last February paid $25 million for British Petroleum's 185,000 barrel-per-day refinery in Marcus Hook, Pennsylvania. After wringing large cost savings from union workers, Tosco agreed to spend $50 million to upgrade the mothballed plant and reopen it next month.

The union official said Tosco plans to cut 67 workers at its Wilmington plant, 43 at its Rodeo plant and four at its Santa Maria operation. Job cuts are not slated at the Carson plant, which is linked to Wilmington by pipeline.
Possible eliminations include the fire and safety units at all four refineries, he said.
Lube production at the Rodeo plant is also on the chopping block in the future, he said. That divisions employs 67 people.
